name: KSambaSharePrivate::add
prose: KSambaSharePrivate::add(shareData) creates or updates a Samba user share. It returns KSambaShareData::UserShareSystemError without running anything if Samba is not installed, and UserShareNameInUse if the data map already holds a share with the same name but a different path. Otherwise it runs 'net usershare add' with the arguments name, path, comment, acl and 'guest_ok=n' when shareData's guest permission is GuestsNotAllowed or 'guest_ok=y' for any other value, collecting standard error into m_stdErr, and logs a warning with the arguments and m_stdErr if that is non-empty. If the process exit code is 0 and the name is not already in the data map, shareData is inserted into the map; an existing entry with the same name and path is left as it is (the process is still run). It returns UserShareOk when the exit code is 0 and UserShareSystemError otherwise.

name: WorkerResult::operator=(const WorkerResult &rhs)
prose: WorkerResult::operator=(const WorkerResult &rhs) returns *this unchanged when this and rhs are the same object. Otherwise it allocates a new WorkerResultPrivate as a copy of *rhs.d (the success flag, error code and error string), stores it in the unique_ptr d (destroying the previous private data) and returns *this. rhs.d is dereferenced, so rhs must not be in a moved-from state (null d); rhs is not modified. The private data is owned by a std::unique_ptr, so it is never shared between objects.

name: WorkerResult::operator=(WorkerResult &&) noexcept = default
prose: The move assignment operator of WorkerResult is defaulted (workerbase.cpp:453): it move-assigns the std::unique_ptr member d, so the previously owned private data is destroyed, d takes over rhs's pointer, and rhs.d becomes null (rhs is then only fit to be assigned to or destroyed). It returns a reference to *this and is declared noexcept. It does not compare against self-assignment itself (that is the unique_ptr's behaviour).

name: KDirOperator::updateSortActions
prose: KDirOperator::updateSortActions() synchronises the sort actions with d->m_sorting; it returns void. It checks, in this order, KFile::isSortByName, isSortByDate, isSortBySize and isSortByType on d->m_sorting and for the first one that holds it calls setChecked(true) on the matching SortBy action and sets the texts of the descending and ascending actions: 'Z-A'/'A-Z' for name and type, 'Newest First'/'Oldest First' for date, 'Largest First'/'Smallest First' for size. If none of the four holds, no sort-by action and no text is changed (an action checked earlier stays checked). In every case it then sets SortAscending checked when QDir::Reversed is clear in d->m_sorting, SortDescending checked when it is set, and SortFoldersFirst checked when QDir::DirsFirst is set.

name: KFilePlacesEventWatcher::eventFilter
prose: KFilePlacesEventWatcher::eventFilter(watched, event) is an inline override defined in kfileplacesview_p.h; watched->parent() is assumed to be the places view (a QAbstractItemView) for the mouse events. It returns true (event consumed) in these cases: a MouseMove while m_isTouchEvent is set and no tap-and-hold is active; a MouseButtonPress while m_isTouchEvent is set; a MouseButtonPress or MouseButtonDblClick at a position that is not a valid index; a left MouseButtonRelease on the teardown action of the index that was clicked (it emits actionClicked first); and a Gesture event (it calls gestureEvent and accepts the event). In all other cases it returns false after its side effects. Side effects: for MouseMove (when not consumed) it clears m_tapAndHoldActive, hides the rubber band if visible, recomputes the hovered header-area and teardown-action indexes and, when either changes, emits headerAreaLeft/headerAreaEntered and actionLeft/actionEntered; for Leave it emits headerAreaLeft and actionLeft for valid hovered indexes and clears both; for MouseButtonPress (not touch) it records the press, the mouse source and calls onPressed; for MouseButtonRelease with the left or middle button it updates the clicked-action index or, for the middle button, emits entryMiddleClicked when the press and release indexes match; WindowActivate, WindowDeactivate and PaletteChange emit windowActivated, windowDeactivated and paletteChanged; TouchBegin sets m_isTouchEvent and clears m_mousePressed.

name: createUDSEntry
prose: Static function createUDSEntry(filename, path, entry, details, fullPath) in file_unix.cpp fills a UDSEntry for the file named by path (a local encoded path); entry must be empty on entry (assert). It returns false when lstat of path fails, or when details includes StatBasic or StatResolveSymlink and the path is a symlink whose target cannot be read (readlinkToBuffer returns empty); entry may already contain UDS_NAME (inserted first when StatBasic is requested) and UDS_LINK_DEST at that point, so it is not left unmodified on false. For a symlink, with StatBasic or StatResolveSymlink it inserts UDS_LINK_DEST; with StatResolveSymlink it also stats the target and, if that fails, treats the link as broken (file type S_IFMT - 1, access 0777, size 0); with StatAcl and POSIX ACL support the ACLs are taken from the link target. It then inserts, depending on details: for StatBasic the file type, access bits and size; for StatAcl the ACL atoms via appendACLAtoms (POSIX ACL builds); for StatUser the local user and group id; for StatTime modification and access time and, where the platform provides a valid birth time, the creation time; for StatInode device and inode number; for StatMimeType the mime type name from QMimeDatabase::mimeTypeForFile(fullPath), or 'inode/directory' when the file type is known to be a directory (the file type is only determined when StatBasic or StatAcl is requested). It returns true when it reaches the end.

name: FtpInternal::ftpOpenDataConnection
prose: FtpInternal::ftpOpenDataConnection() sets up the FTP data connection by trying connection modes in order; it asserts that the session is logged on and first closes any existing data connection. If passive mode is not disabled (config DisablePassiveMode), it tries PASV (ftpOpenPASVDataConnection), returning 0 on success and otherwise remembering the PASV error code and closing the data connection; unless EPSV is disabled it then tries EPSV and returns 0 on success; if an 'EPSV ALL' command was already sent (epsvAllSent), it returns the PASV error code at that point without trying active mode. Otherwise it tries ftpOpenPortDataConnection and returns 0 on success; if that also fails it closes the data connection and returns the PASV error code if there was one, else the error code of the port attempt. The result is 0 or a positive KIO error code (it can be ERR_INTERNAL, since ftpOpenPortDataConnection returns ERR_INTERNAL for a failed port command, contrary to the comment in the source); on active-mode success m_data is not set, only m_server is listening. The caller is responsible for reporting a non-zero result.
note: reviewers right: round1 (positive KIO codes, not < 0), round2 (active-mode success leaves only m_server listening); ftp.cpp:900-942

name: FtpInternal::ftpOpenPortDataConnection
prose: FtpInternal::ftpOpenPortDataConnection() tries to set up an active-mode data connection; m_control must exist and m_data must be null (asserts). It sets m_bPasv to false and returns ERR_INTERNAL immediately, leaving m_server as it is, if EPRT is known to be unsupported (eprtUnknown). Otherwise it creates m_server (a QTcpServer listening on any address, port 0) if there is none; if m_server is not listening it deletes it, sets it to null and returns ERR_CANNOT_LISTEN. It then sets the maximum pending connections to 1 and builds a PORT command from the control connection's IPv4 local address and the server port, or an EPRT command for an IPv6 local address (the command stays empty for any other address family). If sending the command succeeds with a 2xx reply it returns 0, leaving m_server listening and m_data unset; otherwise it deletes m_server, sets it to null and returns ERR_INTERNAL.
note: reviewers right: round1 (eprtUnknown path leaves m_server), round2 (non-IP address family ends with ERR_INTERNAL, not ERR_CANNOT_LISTEN); ftp.cpp:950-996

name: TrashImpl::adaptTrashSize
prose: TrashImpl::adaptTrashSize(origPath, trashId) makes room in the trash for the path origPath according to the trash's settings in ktrashrc (group named by the trash directory): UseTimeLimit (default false), Days (7), UseSizeLimit (true), Percent (10.0) and LimitReachedAction (0). If UseTimeLimit is set it first deletes every trashed file of this trashId whose deletion date is more than Days days before now. If UseSizeLimit is false it returns true. Otherwise it computes the size of origPath and returns true if the usage percentage of (current trash size + that size) relative to the partition is below Percent. It then evaluates util.usage(partitionSize + additionalSize) and, if that is >= Percent, sets m_lastErrorCode to KIO::ERR_TRASH_FILE_TOO_LARGE with its error message and returns false; because usage() is size * 100 / partition size, this value is at least 100 whenever the partition size is non-zero, so with Percent <= 100 control only gets past this check when the partition size is 0. Past that check: LimitReachedAction 0 sets m_lastErrorCode = KIO::ERR_WORKER_DEFINED with a 'trash is full' message and returns false; action 1 or 2 deletes trashed items oldest-first (action 1) or biggest-first (action 2) until the usage including origPath drops below Percent and returns true (also returns true if all items were deleted without reaching it); any other action value prints a warning and returns false without setting m_lastErrorCode or m_lastErrorMessage.
note: reviewer round15 right: the too-large check is util.usage(partitionSize + additionalSize) >= percent (trashimpl.cpp:1326), not 'empty trash plus origPath', and the action paths are practically unreachable for Percent <= 100; original right about the other-action path; trashimpl.cpp:1275-1368

name: KShortUriFilter::filterUri
prose: KShortUriFilter::filterUri(data) const tries to turn the typed string data.typedString() into a URL; it returns true when it set a result (data's filtered URI and URI type, or the error type with an error message) and false when it could not filter the string and leaves data unmodified. The name filterShortUri used in the packet does not exist: the function is KShortUriFilter::filterUri (kshorturifilter.cpp:99-479). Steps in order: extra leading slashes are reduced to one; absolute local paths become file URLs, others are parsed as URLs; with several '@' in the string all but the last are percent-encoded; an unknown protocol followed by a port-like ':' is treated as no protocol. 'start-here:' returns the 'system:/' URL as LocalDir; strings starting with '#', 'man:' or 'info:' return a man:/ or info:/ URL of type Help; a string starting with two backslashes becomes an smb: URL of type NetProtocol. A leading '~' is expanded to the home directory of the current or named user (a user that does not exist or has no home directory yields type Error with a message and returns true), and a leading '$VAR' is expanded from the environment. A '#ref' is split off an existing path. If an absolute directory was supplied in data it is combined with a relative path and checked for existence; a full local path that exists, or whose last component is a wildcard pattern over an existing directory (a name filter), is returned as a local URL: if the 'open' action is not authorized, as LocalFile; a non-directory with execute permission as Executable; a directory or regular file as LocalDir or LocalFile (name filter appended to the path); other file types fall through. If data.checkForExecutables() is set and the first word of the command is found on $PATH, it returns that executable (type Executable, trailing arguments stored with setArguments). A well-formed URL with a known protocol that is not a local full path is returned as Help for man and help and NetProtocol otherwise. If the string has no space, each configured URL hint whose regular expression matches at position 0 yields the hint's URL and type; a protocol-less potential short URL gets the default scheme prepended (and '://' if needed): a valid result is NetProtocol, an invalid one with a known scheme yields type Error with the original URI, and in both cases it returns true (for an invalid URL with an unknown scheme data is left unmodified but true is returned). Finally a full local path that does not exist is returned as LocalFile (for completion); everything else returns false.
note: slice cut the head: real name KShortUriFilter::filterUri; old prose omitted the early branches (start-here:, man/info, UNC, ~ and $ expansion, errors) and the invalid-short-URL-with-unknown-scheme case, which returns true with data unmodified

name: DelegateAnimationHandler::animationState
prose: DelegateAnimationHandler::animationState(option, index, view) returns the hover animation state for an item of the view, creating or updating it as needed. It returns nullptr at once if view is null or the view is in a dragging state. Otherwise it looks up the existing state for (view, index) and whether option has State_MouseOver. If there is no state and the item is hovered it creates and registers a new AnimationState; it starts the animation unless a fade-in was started less than 300 ms ago, in which case it marks it finished in the forward direction (progress 1.0, not animating); it then restarts the fade-in timer and calls eventuallyStartIteration(index). If a state exists and the item is not hovered and the state is not animating or is moving forward, it sets the direction to backward (progress reset to 0 if the state was created less than 200 ms ago), starts the animation and, if index is the sequence index, stops the sequence iteration and clears the sequence index. If a state exists, the item is hovered and the direction is backward, it sets the direction forward, starts the animation if it is not already running and calls eventuallyStartIteration. If there is no state, the item is not hovered and the model reports HasJobRole for the index, it creates and registers a state, starts its animation and marks it as a job animation. In every case it returns the resulting state, which is nullptr if none was found or created.

name: KIO::JobUiDelegate::askDeleteConfirmation
prose: KIO::JobUiDelegate::askDeleteConfirmation(urls, deletionType, confirmationType) asks the user to confirm a delete, trash or empty-trash operation and returns true if the operation may proceed. With confirmationType ForceConfirmation it always asks; otherwise it reads the key ConfirmDelete (default true), ConfirmTrash (default false) or ConfirmEmptyTrash (default true) from the Confirmations group of the kiorc config and asks only if it is true. If it does not ask it returns true. When it asks, it builds a list of display names (for trash: URLs the leading numeric prefix is removed from the path) and shows a KMessageBox continue/cancel warning appropriate for the deletion type and item count, window modal. Afterwards, if the key name is non-empty and the 'Notification Messages' entry for that key in the default config has become false (the user ticked 'do not ask again'), it sets that entry back to true, syncs it and writes false to the key in kiorc's Confirmations group. It returns true if the user chose Continue and false otherwise. The slice named askContinue; that name does not exist (askDeleteConfirmation, jobuidelegate.cpp:178-302).

name: KXErrorHandler::error
prose: KXErrorHandler::error(sync) const returns the handler's was_error flag, which is set by handle() when an X error for this handler's display and for a request at or after the one current when the handler was created was delivered and was counted as an error: with no user handler set every such error counts, with a user handler it counts when that handler returns true (handler1) or non-zero (handler2). name: AppletQuickItemPrivate::compactRepresentationCheck
prose: AppletQuickItemPrivate::compactRepresentationCheck() switches the applet item between its full and compact representation; it returns void. It returns at once, changing nothing, if initComplete is false, if q's width or height is <= 0, if compactRepresentationCheckGuard is already set, or if the current representation already corresponds to appletShouldBeExpanded() (the full item equals currentRepresentationItem when it is true, the compact item equals it when false). Otherwise it sets compactRepresentationCheckGuard for the duration of the function and clears it before returning. If appletShouldBeExpanded() is true: it calls createFullRepresentationItem(); only if that returns a non-null item, the expander item (if any) has its fullRepresentation and compactRepresentation properties cleared and is hidden; fullRepresentationWasVisible is computed as fullRepresentationItem->parentItem() == q; unless the item is q itself it is parented to q and anchored to fill it; the compact item (if any) is hidden; the item becomes currentRepresentationItem and its layout is connected; and if expanded was false and fullRepresentationWasVisible was false, expanded is set to true and expandedChanged(true) is emitted. If it is false: it calls createCompactRepresentationItem() and createCompactRepresentationExpanderItem(), and only if both return non-null items, it makes the compact item visible, parents the expander to q, makes it visible and anchors it to fill q, sets the full representation's parent property to null only if it exists and was parented to q, sets the expander's compactRepresentation to the compact item and clears its fullRepresentation, makes the compact item currentRepresentationItem with its layout connected, and if expanded was true and the full representation had been parented to q, sets expanded to false and emits expandedChanged(false). When a needed creation call returns null, nothing else changes.

name: AppletQuickItem::itemForApplet
prose: Static function AppletQuickItem::itemForApplet(applet) returns the AppletQuickItem of a Plasma::Applet, creating it on first use; the caller must not delete it. It returns nullptr if applet is null. If an item is already cached in s_itemsForApplet it returns that item (this check comes before the shutdown check). Otherwise it returns nullptr if the application is closing down or the applet is destroyed. It then creates a SharedQmlEngine owned by the applet, loads the applet's main script and takes its root object as a ContainmentItem (for containments) or PlasmoidItem (other applets); if the root object has the wrong type and the component has no error it sets a launch error message on the applet. If there is no item, the component has errors or the applet failed to launch, it builds error information (version mismatch messages, QML errors or a missing-package message), logs a warning, loads the shell package's 'appleterror' QML instead and disables the applet's configuration interface; it returns nullptr if that fallback QML itself has errors (without setting a launch error message), and otherwise sets the applet's launch error message to the reason, and returns nullptr if the fallback root object is not a PlasmoidItem (after logging) or else stores the error information in the item's errorInformation property. For an item that was obtained, it stores it in s_itemsForApplet, completes the delayed initialization, marks the applet UI ready (UiReadyConstraint) for non-containments and CustomEmbedded containments, sets the _plasma_applet property, item->d->applet and item->d->qmlObject, sets the 'plasmoid' context property unless PLASMA_NO_CONTEXTPROPERTIES is set, and connects the applet's appletDeleted signal so that the SharedQmlEngine (and with it the item) is deleted and the cache entry removed when the applet is deleted; it also sets the applet's _plasmoid property and returns the item.
